## What changed or decided
- Added `tests/test_paired_invariants.py` (840 lines): 14 `Pair*` classes, one binder per agreement, each with a `*_holds` test (live invariant) and a `*_divergence_*` test (feeds a mutated copy of one side through the same comparison to prove the binder fails when broken — 31 tests total).
- Relation per pair matches each pair's own contract and states it in every message:
  - **Set-equality**: 3 (mirror dirs vs manifest record classes), 5-code (schema/enforcer/loop verdicts), 6 (risk vocab ×7 sites), 7 (code-review verdicts ×4 sites), 9 (memory status/area), 10 (workflow files ×3), 13 (guardian users/label), 14 (smoke/start required).
  - **Containment**: 1 (schema keywords ⊆ implemented), 2 (check literals ⊆ job names), 4 (each PR-body producer ⊇ required headings), 5-prose/workflow (enumerations ⊆ canonical), 8 (default checks ⊆ job names), 12 (referenced ids ⊆ defined). **Subset**: 11 (`required_skill` enum ⊆ `KNOWN_SKILLS`).
- One deliberate deviation from the handoff, resolved to keep it green: pair 3's floor lists `ledger`, but the manifest classifies `.shiki/ledger` as `append-only-evidence`, not `mirror`. Asserting against `state_class: mirror` alone would be red today, so the manifest side is the per-record record classes `{mirror, append-only-evidence}` — the invariant then holds and the docstring/message name why. Bound values are read from source (no hardcoded line numbers), so the tests track drift rather than snapshots.
